therapeutic_hypothesis.proposed_mechanism: MDM2 antagonism to restore p53 function
therapeutic_hypothesis.target_population: Participants with relapsed or refractory acute myeloid leukemia (AML) with TP53 wild-type
therapeutic_hypothesis.primary_endpoint: Overall Survival in TP53 WT Population

subgroup_findings: IDH1 mutation subgroup showed higher CR rate with idasanutlin (34.8% vs 11.1%)
IDH2 mutation subgroup showed modest improvement in CR rate (29.5% vs 23.1%)
FLT3 mutation subgroup showed similar CR rates (15.3% vs 12.5%)
safety_signals: Higher early mortality: 23 deaths by day 30 vs 9 in placebo arm
60 deaths by day 60 vs 24 in placebo arm
Increased laboratory abnormalities including hypophosphatemia, hypocalcemia, hyperuricemia, hyperbilirubinemia
More hematologic toxicities including severe cytopenias
results.dose_information: Idasanutlin 300 mg PO BID (Cycle 1) or QD (Cycles 2-3) for 5 days per cycle, combined with cytarabine 1 g/m² IV for 5 days per cycle

context.duration: Up to 3 cycles of treatment (28 days per cycle), follow-up up to approximately 4.5 years
context.investigator_commentary: Study terminated for futility based on lack of OS benefit and unfavorable benefit-risk profile. The observed marginal benefit does not outweigh the risks of idasanutlin in the relapsed or refractory AML population.
